mechanism: One-time intravitreally delivered recombinant AAV gene therapy using a proprietary capsid and transgene genome encoding the anti-VEGF protein Vb24 to support sustained intraocular anti-angiogenic activity.
phase: Long-term follow-up observational study for Phase 1 and Phase 1/2 parent trials
development_status: NCT06346600 is a recruiting prospective, multicenter, non-interventional 5-year follow-up study enrolling patients who received SKG0106 in parent studies NCT06213038 and NCT05986864. The main U.S./global parent study NCT05986864 is a recruiting Phase 1/2 trial of one-time SKG0106 intravitreal injection in nAMD; no FDA approval or posted ClinicalTrials.gov results were identified.
clinical_summary: SKG0106 is intended to reduce wet AMD treatment burden by replacing repeated anti-VEGF injections with durable intraocular anti-VEGF expression after a single intravitreal AAV administration. NCT06346600 follows 83 exposed patients for ocular/systemic safety and durability measures including BCVA, CST, and VFQ-25 for up to 5 years. Parent NCT05986864 enrolls about 68 nAMD patients into a Phase 1/2 one-time injection study, and parent NCT06213038 enrolls about 12 Chinese patients in Phase 1. An ARVO 2024 interim abstract reported 9 treated patients across 3 dose cohorts, no rescue anti-VEGF injections in the mid- and high-dose cohorts during reported follow-up, and BCVA stabilization or improvement plus CST reduction in those cohorts. Differentiation is meaningful if durability and rescue-free control persist, but evidence remains early, small, open-label, and non-comparative.
safety_summary: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted. NCT06346600's primary endpoint tracks ocular and systemic AEs, SAEs, and AESIs for 5 years after SKG0106 injection, reflecting the long-term safety burden of ocular AAV therapy. The ARVO 2024 interim abstract reported no DLTs or treatment-related SAEs in the low- and mid-dose cohorts through 30-52 weeks and asymptomatic trace mixed vitreous cells in the high-dose cohort that resolved without intervention. Analog intravitreal anti-VEGF labeling supports monitoring for ocular/periocular infection, intraocular inflammation, hypersensitivity, endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, intraocular pressure increases, arterial thromboembolic events, retinal vasculitis/vascular occlusion, cataract, and conjunctival hemorrhage; ocular gene therapy analog labeling adds attention to retinal abnormalities, permanent visual-acuity decline, and corticosteroid-supported immune/inflammation management.
management_tools: Medical-benefit prior authorization tied to FDA-labeled nAMD criteria, active CNV, study-eye documentation, and retina-specialist administration
Per-eye lifetime or one-time quantity limit unless future labeling supports retreatment
Requirement for prior anti-VEGF response, treatment burden, or inadequate durability if final label and evidence support positioning after injectable anti-VEGF therapy
Site-of-care and qualified-injection-center controls for intravitreal gene therapy handling, administration, and post-injection monitoring
Documentation of baseline BCVA, OCT/CST, prior injection frequency, and rescue-injection criteria for continuation/outcomes tracking
Safety monitoring for ocular inflammation, infection, intraocular pressure, retinal abnormalities/detachment, vascular occlusion, and systemic anti-VEGF thromboembolic risk
Outcomes-based contract or amortized payment model consideration if launch price resembles one-time ophthalmic gene therapy analogs
Long-term registry or claims surveillance aligned to 5-year follow-up expectations
evidence_gaps: No FDA approval, U.S. prescribing information, or direct SKG0106 price was identified.
NCT06346600 is observational and administers no investigational product; efficacy and launch assumptions rely on parent studies and interim abstract data.
No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results were identified for NCT06346600, NCT05986864, or NCT06213038.
The ARVO 2024 interim data include only 9 Phase 1 patients with short-to-moderate follow-up and no randomized comparator.

The U.S./global parent study NCT05986864 was last updated January 2025 and had estimated January 2026 completion dates, but remains listed as recruiting in the ClinicalTrials.gov API snapshot reviewed.
A pivotal Phase 3 program, regulatory filing plan, and launch timing have not been identified.
Annual cost estimate uses Luxturna ophthalmic AAV gene therapy analog pricing and may not predict SKG0106 pricing, rebates, bilateral use, administration costs, or outcomes-based payment terms.

expected_launch_window.method: Used NCT05986864 Phase 1/2 status, NCT06346600 5-year follow-up through March 2031, absence of identified Phase 3/filing, and early interim Phase 1 evidence.
expected_launch_window.explanation: SKG0106 is clinically active but still early. Without a pivotal Phase 3 or filing signal, a U.S. launch before 2030 is unlikely; the long-term follow-up requirement reinforces meaningful safety/durability uncertainty.

annual_cost_range.method: No SKG0106 price was found. Used Luxturna, the approved ophthalmic AAV gene therapy analog, at $425,000 per eye and $850,000 for both eyes as a first-year one-time treatment-cost proxy; EYLEA HD WAC is included only as current chronic anti-VEGF benchmark context.
annual_cost_range.explanation: SKG0106 is a one-time ocular AAV therapy, so a one-time per-eye analog is more relevant than annualizing chronic anti-VEGF injections. Final SKG0106 price could differ materially based on durability, bilateral treatment assumptions, outcomes-based contracts, and administration costs.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted one-time intravitreal AAV anti-VEGF mechanism, early rescue-free mid/high dose signal, BCVA/CST stabilization or improvement, and long-term follow-up design against small sample size, open-label design, and lack of randomized pivotal data.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Durable intravitreal anti-VEGF expression could materially reduce injection burden, but the available efficacy and safety evidence is too immature for a High rating.

budget_impact.method: Combined ophthalmic AAV analog one-time cost with a potentially broad nAMD population and medical-benefit/site-of-care complexity.
budget_impact.explanation: Even if restricted to anti-VEGF-experienced or high-burden patients, a per-eye one-time therapy priced like Luxturna would create concentrated claim exposure and demand outcomes-based management.

disruption_risk.method: Balanced high potential to reduce chronic intravitreal injections and alter retina buy-and-bill workflows against early development status, no approval, no direct price, and availability of established anti-VEGF management policies.
disruption_risk.explanation: A durable one-time therapy could disrupt injection frequency, site-of-care economics, and payment design, but near-term disruption is moderated by early clinical maturity and uncertain launch timing.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to Phase 1/2 status, absence of posted results or filing, long-term follow-up through 2031, and early but notable durability signal.
recommended_action.explanation: Track parent study updates, full Phase 1/2 data, rescue-injection durability, ocular inflammation signals, Phase 3 initiation, and any gene-therapy payment model signals. Formal coverage build is premature before pivotal evidence and label details.

quality_flags: Assigned NCT06346600 is a long-term follow-up study and does not administer SKG0106; parent interventional studies were included to characterize development status.
No direct SKG0106 price found; annual cost estimate uses Luxturna ophthalmic AAV gene therapy analog pricing.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for the assigned study or parent studies.
Interim efficacy and safety evidence is based on a small open-label Phase 1 abstract with 9 treated patients and no randomized comparator.
NCT05986864 remains listed as recruiting in the reviewed ClinicalTrials.gov API snapshot despite estimated January 2026 completion dates.
No Phase 3, BLA filing, FDA label, or U.S. launch date was identified.
